knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Gradient of a Function of Three Variables

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{xyz}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{xyz}}\cdot (yz) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{xyz}}{2x} \\ {f}_{y}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{xyz}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{xyz}}\cdot (xz) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{xyz}}{2y} \\ {f}_{z}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\sqrt{xyz}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{xyz}}\cdot (xy) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{xyz}}{2z}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the gradient is:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\text{ }i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{xyz}}{2x}\text{ }i+\frac{\sqrt{xyz}}{2y}\text{ }j+\frac{\sqrt{xyz}}{2z}\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{xyz}}{2}(\frac{1}{x}\text{ }i+\frac{1}{y}\text{ }j+\frac{1}{z}\text{ }k)\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{x+2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{yz})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x+2}}+0 \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x+2}} \\ {g}_{y}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{x+2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{yz})) \\  & =0+\frac{1}{\sqrt{yz}}\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{yz}}\cdot z \\  & =\frac{1}{2y} \\ {g}_{z}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\sqrt{x+2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\sqrt{yz})) \\  & =0+\frac{1}{\sqrt{yz}}\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{yz}}\cdot y \\  & =\frac{1}{2z}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,  the gradient is:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y,z) & ={g}_{x}(x,y,z)\text{ }i+{g}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{g}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x+2}}i+\frac{1}{2y}\text{ }j+\frac{1}{2z}\text{ }k\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{y}+{y}^{z}) \\  & =y{x}^{y-1} \\ {f}_{y}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{y}+{y}^{z}) \\  & ={x}^{y}\operatorname{ln}⁡x+z{y}^{z-1} \\ {f}_{z}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{y}+{y}^{z}) \\  & ={y}^{z}\operatorname{ln}⁡y\end{aligned}

Hence, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =y{x}^{y-1}\,i+({x}^{y}\operatorname{ln}⁡x+z{y}^{z-1})j+{y}^{z}\operatorname{ln}⁡y\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $∇g(x,y,z)$ at the point $(1,3,1)$ if $g(x,y,z)=- \frac{x y z}{3 x + y + z}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(- \frac{x y z}{3 x + y + z}) \\  & =\frac{(3 x + y + z)(- y z)-(- x y z)(3)}{(3 x + y + z)^2} \\  & =- \frac{y z \left(y + z\right)}{\left(3 x + y + z\right)^{2}} \\ {g}_{y}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(- \frac{x y z}{3 x + y + z}) \\  & =\frac{(3 x + y + z)(- x z)-(- x y z)(1)}{(3 x + y + z)^2} \\  & =- \frac{x z \left(3 x + z\right)}{\left(3 x + y + z\right)^{2}} \\ {g}_{z}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(- \frac{x y z}{3 x + y + z}) \\  & =\frac{(3 x + y + z)(- x y)-(- x y z)(1)}{(3 x + y + z)^2} \\  & =- \frac{x y \left(3 x + y\right)}{\left(3 x + y + z\right)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y,z) & ={g}_{x}(x,y,z)\,\mathbf i+{g}_{y}(x,y,z)\,\mathbf j+{g}_{z}(x,y,z)\,\mathbf k \\  & =(\frac{3 x y z}{\left(3 x + y + z\right)^{2}} - \frac{y z}{3 x + y + z})\,\mathbf i+(\frac{x y z}{\left(3 x + y + z\right)^{2}} - \frac{x z}{3 x + y + z})\,\mathbf j+(\frac{x y z}{\left(3 x + y + z\right)^{2}} - \frac{x y}{3 x + y + z})\,\mathbf k \\ ∇g(1,3,1) & =(\frac{(7)(-3)-(-3)(3)}{(7)^2})\,\mathbf i+(\frac{(7)(-1)-(-3)(1)}{(7)^2})\,\mathbf j+(\frac{(7)(-3)-(-3)(1)}{(7)^2})\,\mathbf k \\  & =(- \frac{12}{49})\,\mathbf i+(- \frac{4}{49})\,\mathbf j+(- \frac{18}{49})\,\mathbf k \\  & =(- \frac{12}{49})\,\mathbf i+(- \frac{4}{49})\,\mathbf j+(- \frac{18}{49})\,\mathbf k\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $∇g(x,y,z)$ at the point $(3,1,3)$ if $g(x,y,z)=- \frac{2 x y z}{3 x - y + z}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(- \frac{2 x y z}{3 x - y + z}) \\  & =\frac{(3 x - y + z)(- 2 y z)-(- 2 x y z)(3)}{(3 x - y + z)^2} \\  & =\frac{2 y z \left(y - z\right)}{\left(3 x - y + z\right)^{2}} \\ {g}_{y}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(- \frac{2 x y z}{3 x - y + z}) \\  & =\frac{(3 x - y + z)(- 2 x z)-(- 2 x y z)(-1)}{(3 x - y + z)^2} \\  & =- \frac{2 x z \left(3 x + z\right)}{\left(3 x - y + z\right)^{2}} \\ {g}_{z}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(- \frac{2 x y z}{3 x - y + z}) \\  & =\frac{(3 x - y + z)(- 2 x y)-(- 2 x y z)(1)}{(3 x - y + z)^2} \\  & =- \frac{2 x y \left(3 x - y\right)}{\left(3 x - y + z\right)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y,z) & ={g}_{x}(x,y,z)\,\mathbf i+{g}_{y}(x,y,z)\,\mathbf j+{g}_{z}(x,y,z)\,\mathbf k \\  & =(\frac{6 x y z}{\left(3 x - y + z\right)^{2}} - \frac{2 y z}{3 x - y + z})\,\mathbf i+(- \frac{2 x y z}{\left(3 x - y + z\right)^{2}} - \frac{2 x z}{3 x - y + z})\,\mathbf j+(\frac{2 x y z}{\left(3 x - y + z\right)^{2}} - \frac{2 x y}{3 x - y + z})\,\mathbf k \\ ∇g(3,1,3) & =(\frac{(11)(-6)-(-18)(3)}{(11)^2})\,\mathbf i+(\frac{(11)(-18)-(-18)(-1)}{(11)^2})\,\mathbf j+(\frac{(11)(-6)-(-18)(1)}{(11)^2})\,\mathbf k \\  & =(- \frac{12}{121})\,\mathbf i+(- \frac{216}{121})\,\mathbf j+(- \frac{48}{121})\,\mathbf k \\  & =(- \frac{12}{121})\,\mathbf i+(- \frac{216}{121})\,\mathbf j+(- \frac{48}{121})\,\mathbf k\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $∇g(x,y,z)$ at the point $(-1,-3,1)$ if $g(x,y,z)=- \frac{3 x y z}{- 2 x - 3 y + z}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(- \frac{3 x y z}{- 2 x - 3 y + z}) \\  & =\frac{(- 2 x - 3 y + z)(- 3 y z)-(- 3 x y z)(-2)}{(- 2 x - 3 y + z)^2} \\  & =\frac{3 y z \left(3 y - z\right)}{\left(2 x + 3 y - z\right)^{2}} \\ {g}_{y}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(- \frac{3 x y z}{- 2 x - 3 y + z}) \\  & =\frac{(- 2 x - 3 y + z)(- 3 x z)-(- 3 x y z)(-3)}{(- 2 x - 3 y + z)^2} \\  & =\frac{3 x z \left(2 x - z\right)}{\left(2 x + 3 y - z\right)^{2}} \\ {g}_{z}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(- \frac{3 x y z}{- 2 x - 3 y + z}) \\  & =\frac{(- 2 x - 3 y + z)(- 3 x y)-(- 3 x y z)(1)}{(- 2 x - 3 y + z)^2} \\  & =\frac{3 x y \left(2 x + 3 y\right)}{\left(2 x + 3 y - z\right)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y,z) & ={g}_{x}(x,y,z)\,\mathbf i+{g}_{y}(x,y,z)\,\mathbf j+{g}_{z}(x,y,z)\,\mathbf k \\  & =(- \frac{6 x y z}{\left(- 2 x - 3 y + z\right)^{2}} - \frac{3 y z}{- 2 x - 3 y + z})\,\mathbf i+(- \frac{9 x y z}{\left(- 2 x - 3 y + z\right)^{2}} - \frac{3 x z}{- 2 x - 3 y + z})\,\mathbf j+(\frac{3 x y z}{\left(- 2 x - 3 y + z\right)^{2}} - \frac{3 x y}{- 2 x - 3 y + z})\,\mathbf k \\ ∇g(-1,-3,1) & =(\frac{(12)(9)-(-9)(-2)}{(12)^2})\,\mathbf i+(\frac{(12)(3)-(-9)(-3)}{(12)^2})\,\mathbf j+(\frac{(12)(-9)-(-9)(1)}{(12)^2})\,\mathbf k \\  & =(\frac{5}{8})\,\mathbf i+(\frac{1}{16})\,\mathbf j+(- \frac{11}{16})\,\mathbf k \\  & =(\frac{5}{8})\,\mathbf i+(\frac{1}{16})\,\mathbf j+(- \frac{11}{16})\,\mathbf k\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find $∇g(x,y,z)$ given that $g(x,y,z)=2 x^{3} + 2 y^{3} + 2 z^{2}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2 x^{3} + 2 y^{3} + 2 z^{2}) \\  & =(6 x^{2})+(0)+(0) \\  & =6 x^{2} \\ {g}_{y}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2 x^{3} + 2 y^{3} + 2 z^{2}) \\  & =(0)+(6 y^{2})+(0) \\  & =6 y^{2} \\ {g}_{z}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(2 x^{3} + 2 y^{3} + 2 z^{2}) \\  & =(0)+(0)+(4 z) \\  & =4 z\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y,z) & ={g}_{x}(x,y,z)\,\mathbf i+{g}_{y}(x,y,z)\,\mathbf j+{g}_{z}(x,y,z)\,\mathbf k \\  & =(6 x^{2})\,\mathbf i+(6 y^{2})\,\mathbf j+(4 z)\,\mathbf k\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $∇g(x,y,z)$ at the point $(-2,-3,-3)$ if $g(x,y,z)=\frac{x y z}{2 x + 3 y + z}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x y z}{2 x + 3 y + z}) \\  & =\frac{(2 x + 3 y + z)(y z)-(x y z)(2)}{(2 x + 3 y + z)^2} \\  & =\frac{y z \left(3 y + z\right)}{\left(2 x + 3 y + z\right)^{2}} \\ {g}_{y}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x y z}{2 x + 3 y + z}) \\  & =\frac{(2 x + 3 y + z)(x z)-(x y z)(3)}{(2 x + 3 y + z)^2} \\  & =\frac{x z \left(2 x + z\right)}{\left(2 x + 3 y + z\right)^{2}} \\ {g}_{z}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{x y z}{2 x + 3 y + z}) \\  & =\frac{(2 x + 3 y + z)(x y)-(x y z)(1)}{(2 x + 3 y + z)^2} \\  & =\frac{x y \left(2 x + 3 y\right)}{\left(2 x + 3 y + z\right)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y,z) & ={g}_{x}(x,y,z)\,\mathbf i+{g}_{y}(x,y,z)\,\mathbf j+{g}_{z}(x,y,z)\,\mathbf k \\  & =(- \frac{2 x y z}{\left(2 x + 3 y + z\right)^{2}} + \frac{y z}{2 x + 3 y + z})\,\mathbf i+(- \frac{3 x y z}{\left(2 x + 3 y + z\right)^{2}} + \frac{x z}{2 x + 3 y + z})\,\mathbf j+(- \frac{x y z}{\left(2 x + 3 y + z\right)^{2}} + \frac{x y}{2 x + 3 y + z})\,\mathbf k \\ ∇g(-2,-3,-3) & =(\frac{(-16)(9)-(-18)(2)}{(-16)^2})\,\mathbf i+(\frac{(-16)(6)-(-18)(3)}{(-16)^2})\,\mathbf j+(\frac{(-16)(6)-(-18)(1)}{(-16)^2})\,\mathbf k \\  & =(- \frac{27}{64})\,\mathbf i+(- \frac{21}{128})\,\mathbf j+(- \frac{39}{128})\,\mathbf k \\  & =(- \frac{27}{64})\,\mathbf i+(- \frac{21}{128})\,\mathbf j+(- \frac{39}{128})\,\mathbf k\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
